Definition: {to grave, by implication, to write (describe, inscribe, prescribe, subscribe)}
BiblicalUsage: Kethab means to write, to grave, to inscribe: Ezra 5:7 says they sent a letter unto Darius, wherein was written thus, unto Darius the king, all peace. Daniel 5:5 says fingers of a man's hand wrote over against the candlestick upon the plaister of the wall. Daniel 6:25 says king Darius wrote unto all people, nations, and languages, Peace be multiplied unto you. Daniel 7:1 says Daniel wrote the dream, and told the sum of the matters.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe writing fixes what men say: a letter to a king, a decree to all nations, a dream told in full, and a hand writing on a wall. I hold that God writes too, and his writing outlasts every king's.
